entry.content: Payment platforms operate in a demanding environment. They must protect payment account data and support the teams that authorize transactions, investigate suspicious activity, and resolve exceptions. The more people and systems that can see sensitive data, the harder it is to control exposure. And the more data is locked away, the harder it can be to use in legitimate workflows. So how can you set up the platforms to ensure they protect that data while also giving the right people access?

entry.content: Enterprise workloads are getting bigger, more variable, and harder to predict, especially as agentic applications introduce spiky, unpredictable demand. Most data platforms weren't built for this reality—to cope with demand, they bolt AI services onto aging architecture, leaving customers to manage, monitor, and pay for multiple systems to get the job done. That fragmentation slows your teams down and limits how fast and how far your agentic applications can run.
